limitations_and_boundaries: Organoid formation efficiency from single Lgr5-GFPhi cells is low (~6%), with most cells dying within 12 h, likely due to isolation stress.
Culture requires exogenous factors (EGF, R-spondin 1, Noggin) and Matrigel, which may not fully recapitulate the in vivo niche.
Small intercellular vacuoles observed by electron microscopy may indicate culture- or fixation-induced stress.
Experiments performed in mouse; human relevance not addressed.
Long-term genetic stability not comprehensively assessed beyond karyotype (40 chromosomes).

research_questions.statement: Can single Lgr5+ stem cells build crypt-villus structures in vitro without a mesenchymal niche?

provenance.text_excerpt: We conclude that intestinal crypt–villus units are self-organizing structures, which can be built from a single stem cell in the absence of a non-epithelial cellular niche.

claims.statement: Intestinal crypt-villus units are self-organizing structures that can be built from a single stem cell in the absence of a non-epithelial cellular niche.

evidence_spans.content: The cultured crypts behaved in a stereotypical manner. The upper opening rapidly became sealed, and the lumen filled with apoptotic cells. The crypt region underwent continuous budding events, reminiscent of crypt fission.

provenance.text_excerpt: The cultured crypts behaved in a stereotypical manner (Fig. 1a; Supplementary Movie 1). The upper opening rapidly became sealed, and the lumen filled with apoptotic cells. The crypt region underwent continuous budding events, reminiscent of crypt fission.

experiments_or_tasks: Assess Wnt signaling by nuclear β-catenin and target gene expression.
Confirm absence of non-epithelial cells by immunostaining and electron microscopy.
Establish long-term culture of isolated mouse small-intestinal crypts in Matrigel with EGF, R-spondin 1, and Noggin.
Monitor growth, budding, and differentiation over 8 months.
Perform lineage tracing using Lgr5-EGFP-ires-CreERT2;Rosa26-LacZ or Rosa26-YFP mice.

methods.name: Crypt isolation and culture
methods.protocol_description: Crypts released from murine small intestine by 30 min incubation in PBS/2 mM EDTA at 4°C. 500 crypts embedded in 50 µl Matrigel per well (24-well plate). Culture medium: Advanced DMEM/F12 with EGF (10–50 ng/ml), R-spondin 1 (500 ng/ml), Noggin (100 ng/ml). Medium changed every 4 days; growth factors added every other day. Passaged every 1–2 weeks at 1:5 split by mechanical dissociation.

methods.name: Lineage tracing
methods.protocol_description: Crypts from Lgr5-EGFP-ires-CreERT2 crossed with Rosa26-LacZ or Rosa26-YFP reporter mice. Induced with 100 nM 4-hydroxytamoxifen for 12 h. X-Gal staining or YFP fluorescence monitored over days.

methods.name: Immunostaining and microscopy
methods.protocol_description: Whole-mount or paraffin sections. Antibodies: anti-lysozyme, anti-synaptophysin, anti-chromogranin A, anti-Muc2, anti-villin, anti-E-cadherin, anti-β-catenin, anti-EphB2. Confocal (Leica SP5), inverted (Nikon DM-IL), stereo (Leica MZ16-FA) microscopy. Electron microscopy: fixed in Karnovsky’s fixative, embedded in Epon, examined with Phillips CM10.

methods.name: Single cell sorting and culture
methods.protocol_description: Crypts dissociated by incubation in culture medium 45 min at 37°C, trituration, filtered through 20 µm strainer. Lgr5-GFPhi, GFPlow, GFP- cells sorted by flow cytometry (MoFlo). Single cells embedded in 5 µl Matrigel per well (96-well plate) with Jagged-1 peptide (1 µM). Culture medium: Advanced DMEM/F12 with EGF, R-spondin 1, Noggin, and Y-27632 (10 µM). Growth factors added every other day; medium changed every 4 days.

methods.name: EdU incorporation assay
methods.protocol_description: Organoids cultured with EdU (thymidine analogue) for 1 h, then stained following Click-iT protocol.

study_units.name: Single Lgr5+ stem cell organoid formation

provenance.text_excerpt: By four days of culture, the structures consisted of about 100 cells

Fully polarized enterocytes, as demonstrated by villin+ mature brush borders and apical alkaline phosphatase, lined the central lumen. Goblet cells (Muc2+, PAS+) and enteroendocrine cells (chromogranin A+, synaptophysin+) were scattered throughout the organoid structure. Four types of mature cell were recognized by electron microscopy.
